We know that 1 liter of oxygen consumed corresponds to approximately 21 kJ of energy under steady-state aerobic conditions.  

Oxygen uptake = \( 3.0 \, \text{l/min} \times 5 \, \text{min} = 15 \, \text{liters} \) of oxygen.  

Energy = \( 15 \times 21 \, \text{kJ} = 315 \, \text{kJ} \).  

This is closest to 300 kJ among the options.  

Final answer: (C)
